legend: Wandering past the fresh produce, Busy Beaver's attention is captured by the local dairy vendor with a peculiar board game at his stall.

There is a circular board with N$$$N$$$ squares numbered from 0$$$0$$$ to N−1$$$N-1$$$. Busy Beaver plays a game on this board with an N$$$N$$$ sided die labelled from 0$$$0$$$ to N−1$$$N-1$$$. If he is on square s$$$s$$$ and moves by t$$$t$$$ steps, he will land directly on the square s+t(modN)$$$s+t \pmod N$$$.
There is also one magical portal on the board, such that if the player lands exactly on square X$$$X$$$, they are instantly teleported to square Y$$$Y$$$.

Busy Beaver rolls the die K$$$K$$$ times and obtains the sequence a1,a2,…,aK$$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_K$$$. From his initial square, Busy Beaver will move by a1$$$a_1$$$ steps, then by a2$$$a_2$$$ steps, and so on until he has completed all K$$$K$$$ moves, where he moves by ai$$$a_i$$$ on the i$$$i$$$-th move.

For each possible initial square from 0$$$0$$$ to N−1$$$N-1$$$ (inclusive, except square X$$$X$$$), determine the square that Busy Beaver lands on after all K$$$K$$$ moves are completed (including any teleports).
input: The first line contains the number of test cases T$$$T$$$ (1≤T≤2⋅103$$$1 \le T \le 2 \cdot 10^3$$$).

The first line of each test case contains four integers N$$$N$$$, K$$$K$$$, X$$$X$$$, and Y$$$Y$$$ (2≤N≤5⋅105$$$2 \le N \le 5 \cdot 10^5$$$, 1≤K≤5⋅105$$$1 \le K \le 5 \cdot 10^5$$$, 0≤X,Y<N$$$0 \le X, Y  \lt  N$$$, X≠Y$$$X \ne Y$$$).
The second line of each test case contains K$$$K$$$ integers a1,a2,…,aK$$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_K$$$ (0≤ai<N$$$0 \le a_i  \lt  N$$$).
The sum of N$$$N$$$ across all test cases does not exceed 5⋅105$$$5 \cdot 10^5$$$.
The sum of K$$$K$$$ across all test cases does not exceed 5⋅105$$$5 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output: For each test case, output N−1$$$N-1$$$ integers representing the square that Busy Beaver would land on if he started on square i$$$i$$$, for all 0≤i<N$$$0 \le i  \lt  N$$$ except for i=X$$$i = X$$$.
There are two subtasks for this problem.
(20$$$20$$$ points): The sum of N$$$N$$$ across all test cases does not exceed 5⋅103$$$5 \cdot 10^3$$$, and the sum of K$$$K$$$ across all test cases does not exceed 5⋅103$$$5 \cdot 10^3$$$.
note: In the first sample test case, there are 5$$$5$$$ squares on the board and one die roll that rolls 1$$$1$$$. The portal teleports the player from square 0$$$0$$$ to square 1$$$1$$$. For each of the starting squares, here is the sequence of events:
0$$$0$$$: The portal teleports from this square; we do not need to output anything.
1$$$1$$$: starts on square 1$$$1$$$, moves by 1$$$1$$$ to square 2$$$2$$$
2$$$2$$$: starts on square 2$$$2$$$, moves by 1$$$1$$$ to square 3$$$3$$$
3$$$3$$$: starts on square 3$$$3$$$, moves by 1$$$1$$$ to square 4$$$4$$$
4$$$4$$$: starts on square 4$$$4$$$, moves by 1$$$1$$$ to square 0$$$0$$$ and teleports to square 1$$$1$$$

In the second sample test case, there are 5$$$5$$$ squares on the board and three die rolls that roll 1,2,3$$$1,2,3$$$ respectively. The portal teleports the player from square 0$$$0$$$ to square 1$$$1$$$. For each of the starting squares, here is the sequence of events:
0$$$0$$$: The portal teleports from this square; we do not need to output anything.
1$$$1$$$: starts on square 1$$$1$$$, moves by 1$$$1$$$ to square 2$$$2$$$, moves by 2$$$2$$$ to square 4$$$4$$$, moves by 3$$$3$$$ to square 2$$$2$$$
2$$$2$$$: starts on square 2$$$2$$$, moves by 1$$$1$$$ to square 3$$$3$$$, moves by 2$$$2$$$ to square 0$$$0$$$ and teleports to square 1$$$1$$$, moves by 3$$$3$$$ to square 4$$$4$$$
3$$$3$$$: starts on square 3$$$3$$$, moves by 1$$$1$$$ to square 4$$$4$$$, moves by 2$$$2$$$ to square 1$$$1$$$, moves by 3$$$3$$$ to square 4$$$4$$$
4$$$4$$$: starts on square 4$$$4$$$, moves by 1$$$1$$$ to square 0$$$0$$$ and teleports to square 1$$$1$$$, moves by 2$$$2$$$ to square 3$$$3$$$, moves by 3$$$3$$$ to square 1$$$1$$$
